minutes.summary: The Board of Trust Fund Commissioners (two members, John Bowen and Richard Howard) spent nearly the entire meeting on a detailed breach notice alleging the Town of Lunenburg has failed for over 50 years to properly administer, document, and distribute numerous charitable trust funds, including missing donor declarations, an entirely missing fund, and unresolved American Legion fund eligibility requirements. The board voted to send a letter and submission packet to the Attorney General's Division of Public Charities and to the Town Manager and Select Board, giving the town 30 days to act, and also voted to amend the operating policy for the American Legion funds and adopt signature-page documents to formalize the filings. Chair Bowen also raised in commission comment concerns about the town's proposed override and his own re-election filing for the board.

what_happened.line: The commission voted to send town officials a breach notice alleging decades of mismanagement of charitable trust funds, starting a cure period before the Attorney General's office is notified.
Members separately voted to approve the letter itself describing the town's failures as trustee of those funds.
The board voted to update eligibility rules for the American Legion trust funds to match the American Legion's own constitution.
Review of a backlog of past meeting minutes was postponed to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: This touches the town's legal duty as trustee over several named charitable funds -- including one the commission says is missing entirely -- and could expose the town to a state complaint or a repayment demand.

Residents should watch whether the Town Manager and Select Board respond within the cure period the commission set, since no response could lead to a formal referral to the Attorney General's Division of Public Charities.
